dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hello, yes, good afternoon. This is Isabel Teixeira. I'm calling because the streetlights are out again on my street. Well, not again, I shouldn't say that, but it's a nuisance, I'll tell you.
I'm sorry about that, Mrs. Teixeira. Which street are you on?
Gidley Street. Three thirty-six Gidley Street, in the Fifth Ward. The whole block went dark last night. Every light, from the corner down to the end. Pitch black. You couldn't see your own steps.
Okay, 336 Gidley Street. The whole block, so not just one light. Was that last night, Monday night?

Monday night, yes. Went out around, oh, suppose it was after supper. And it's a shame, because when I was a girl, the lamplighter, no, that's not right, that was my mother's time, they had the gas ones on Thames Street. She used to tell me, they'd come along with a long pole and, oh. I'm sorry, dear. I wander.
That's all right. Did the lights come back on at all, or are they still out?
Well, they're daytime now, so I can't tell you. Hold on. [pause] What? No, I'm getting to it. My grandson is here whispering at me over my shoulder.
That's fine, take your time.

He says tell them it's the pole. He says there's a pole by the corner that buzzes. I said I know, I know, let me say it. He's fifteen, he thinks I can't run a telephone. Now he's saying ask for a crew. Yes, I was going to!
He's got good suggestions. So there's a buzzing pole near the corner? Do you know if it's the one at the end of Gidley, or closer to your house?
Closer to the corner, he says. The one at the end by the stop sign. Not mine, mine's the one across from the house, that one's just dark like the rest.

Got it. I'll write down that the whole block on Gidley Street lost power to the lights Monday night, and there's a pole near the corner by the stop sign that's been buzzing. And you'd like a crew to go check that pole. Did I get that right?
That's right, that's exactly it. Please send somebody to look at it. It's dangerous for people walking, and some of us don't see so well anymore, and I don't want to fall on my own steps.
Understood. I'll put in the request for a crew to check the pole and the lights on the block. Is 401-555-0154 the best number if they need to reach you?
Yes, that's the house phone. Oh, he's saying it's too slow. I said it's a phone call, Mateus, that's how it works. Sorry.

No trouble at all. Crews check these as they come in, so you should see someone out there in the next few days. If the lights are still out tonight, or the buzzing gets louder or you see sparks, call back and let us know right away.
Sparks. Oh, dear, he didn't say anything about sparks. Well, I'll watch. Thank you, Lorraine. It's an aggravation, that's all, a whole street in the dark.
I know. We'll get it looked at. Thanks for calling, Mrs. Teixeira. Take care.
You too, dear. Goodbye.
